senses.gloss:
dagdhayoga
------------------------------------------
Right from the Vedic days Hindus have been rather fastidious in choosing ‘good’ days and avoiding ‘bad’ days for the starting of any venture. Even now, even the average Hindu, is very particular about this.
Such days are generally decided with the help of astrologers and priests who consult the पञ्चाङ्ग (the almanac) and give their opinion. One of the inauspicious days mentioned there, is called ‘dagdha-योग’. If the week days from Sunday to Saturday occur on certain tithis (days as per the lunar चलेन्दर्) as shown below, they are called ‘dagdhayogas’. The name is perhaps derived from the reason that ventures started on such days of the week, united (yoga = union) with certain tithis, become dagdha or destroyed (dagdha = burnt, destroyed).
They are:
Sunday associated with dvādaśī (12th day)
Monday associated with ekādaśī (11th day)
Tuesday associated with daśamī (10th day)
Wednesday associated with tṛtīyā (3rd day)
Thursday associated with ṣaṣṭhī (6th day)
Friday associated with dvitīyā (2nd day)
Saturday associated with saptamī (7th day)

The days (or tithis) given in the last column are calculated either from the day after the new-मोओन् or the full-मोओन्.
These दग्धयोग days are inauspicious.
